entries.clue: Polar animal's stomach? (4)

blocks.note: a verb here: to tolerate or endure

annotation.surface: A question about what an Arctic creature's belly is like.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, but it is 'is': the polar animal IS stomach, and 'stomach' is a verb meaning tolerate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun for the animal paired with a verb sense: to put up with something unpleasant, as in 'I can't stomach it'.

entries.clue: Dilapidated sideboards getting batterings (10)

indicatorNotes.Dilapidated: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Some worn-out old furniture taking a further beating.
annotation.walkthrough: Sideboards also means side-whiskers, but here it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a broadside is a full volley of a ship's guns, and figuratively a fierce verbal attack.

entries.clue: So, hardware flying around? (10)

indicatorNotes.flying around: letters flying around land in a new order

annotation.surface: A remark about metal objects whizzing through the air.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the answer is metal hardware that flies around, and the letters of SO HARDWARE fly into it.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the metal points of arrows are hardware that does literally fly around.

entries.clue: Performing culinary operation on – foolishly – rock pigeon (10)

indicatorNotes.foolishly: letters arranged foolishly are in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Someone making a silly job of cooking a rock pigeon.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'on' look like part of the fodder, but it belongs to the definition, which needs an object.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: cooking something partly in advance is an operation carried out on food.

entries.clue: Region including villas in exclusive resort areas, primarily? (7)

annotation.definition: Region including villas in exclusive resort areas

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily = in first place, so take each word's first letter

blocks.clueFragment: Region including villas in exclusive resort areas
blocks.note: first letters of the seven words

annotation.surface: A description of a coastline lined with smart villas and upmarket resorts.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word before 'primarily' contributes its first letter, and the same words describe the answer, so the whole clue is also the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the French and Italian coastline is the classic region of villas and exclusive resorts.

entries.clue: Blearily recalls wine in large amounts (7)

indicatorNotes.Blearily: a bleary memory gets things jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone hazily remembering how much they drank.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink in the surface explains the bleariness, but 'recalls' is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by extension: a cellar is a householder's store of wine, so several are wine kept in quantity.

entries.clue: Ministry of Defence to get 'non-clerical' if Foreign Office to retire bureaucrats (11)

indicatorNotes.to retire: to retire is to draw back, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: MOD = Ministry of Defence, the UK's armed-forces department
laic = of the laity, not clergy
FO = Foreign Office, the UK's foreign ministry

annotation.surface: A sentence of civil-service jargon about reshuffling departments.
annotation.walkthrough: Build MOD LAIC IF FO in clue order, then read the whole string backwards. 'To get' only joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the word names officials as a body, especially when seen as bureaucratic.

entries.clue: Everyman is to receive visitor, finally: one bearing large showy flowers (4)

indicatorNotes.to receive: to receive a visitor is to take them in, so R goes inside
indicatorNotes.finally: finally = at the end, so only the last letter of visitor is used

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself, so Everyman = I

annotation.surface: The setter announcing that he is expecting a guest.
annotation.walkthrough: I + IS receives R between its parts. Setters routinely call themselves I or ME by their pen name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the garden flag is known for tall stems of big, showy blooms.

entries.clue: Celt's outburst can be heard (4)

indicatorNotes.can be heard: the word is identified by its sound

blocks.note: a gale of laughter is an outburst

annotation.surface: A Celtic person shouting loudly enough for everyone to hear.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', not a possessive: the Celt is an outburst, said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Gaelic-speaking Scot or Irishman is one kind of Celt.

entries.clue: In conversation, much time shared by you and me (4)

indicatorNotes.In conversation: in speech, so go by the sound

blocks.note: hours = much time; its H is silent

annotation.surface: A remark that two people have spent a lot of time talking together.
annotation.walkthrough: HOURS and the answer sound the same because the H of hour is never spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the possessive pronoun for what belongs to both speaker and listener.

entries.clue: Eggs and lice covering rancid president's workplace (4,6)

indicatorNotes.covering: LICE covers OFF, going round it

blocks.note: used as it stands, split L…ICE

annotation.surface: A grim description of a dirty, verminous room belonging to a president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' just joins OVA to the L(OFF)ICE unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Proper name: the oval-shaped room in the White House where the US president works.

entries.clue: Cheers that man, earlier sad, starting to brood (4,3,5)

indicatorNotes.starting: starting = the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: down = sad; 'earlier' puts it at the front
to hatch is to brood eggs, or a brood

annotation.surface: A man who was downcast beginning to sit and mope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starting to' is the first letter of to, not an instruction; the pieces are laid out so DOWN, then T and HE, lead into HATCH.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a jokey toast said before downing a drink, used just like 'Cheers'.

entries.clue: Champion with spine, usually? (5-6)

blocks.note: a sporting champion, current owner of the crown
the spine of a book, which usually carries its name

annotation.surface: A champion praised for having backbone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spine' suggests courage in a champion, but it is the spine of a book, which usually holds the title.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for a sporting champion, plus a literal reading: a book's spine carries the name printed on it.

entries.clue: Note, twice: establishment for racehorses where multiplication is demanded (5,5)

blocks.note: ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a second note: me, a spelling of mi
racehorses are trained at a stable

annotation.surface: A racing stable where the horses are made to do arithmetic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note, twice' means two different sol-fa notes, TI and ME, not the same note repeated.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the chart pupils learn by heart, where the answers to multiplication are asked for.

entries.clue: Hot drinks or dry Rieslings? (4,6)

blocks.note: espresso coffees topped with velvety steamed milk
Riesling is a white wine; read 'dry' as dull and lifeless, like a drink gone still

annotation.surface: A choice of drinks: coffee or a crisp white wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' suggests unsweet wine, but the joke is lifeless white wines.
annotation.definitionFit: The coffee is a proper name for an espresso with steamed milk; the wine reading takes the first word as lifeless and the second as white wine.

entries.clue: Sluggishness, batting: time to win it back? (7)

indicatorNotes.to win: to win something is to gain it, taking it in
indicatorNotes.back: back = in reverse, so IT turns round

blocks.note: a batter in cricket is in
era = a period of time, split ER…A

annotation.surface: A sluggish batsman in cricket hoping to claw back the match.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in', and a batsman at the crease is in. ERA wins TI.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a physics term for resistance to motion, used generally for sluggishness.

entries.clue: Dog's cross: that is, a little labradoodle (7)

indicatorNotes.a little: just a little of the word: its first letter

blocks.note: to span a river is to cross it

annotation.surface: A remark that a labradoodle, being a crossbreed, is a bit of a mongrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' in a dog clue points at crossbreeds like the labradoodle, but it is the verb span. 'Dog's' means 'dog is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the answer is one breed of gundog.

entries.clue: Unbroken, like a Manx cat? (7)

blocks.note: the Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, has no tail

annotation.surface: A remark about a tailless cat that has never been hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: The Manx cat is a breed from the Isle of Man that has no tail, so it has no end.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for continuous, plus a literal reading: a Manx cat lacks its tail end.

entries.clue: I will be found in Balkan state: bold to move to find unwelcoming place (7)

indicatorNotes.will be found in: to be found in something is to sit inside it, so I goes into SERBIA
indicatorNotes.to move: to move is to change place, so the B shifts along the word

blocks.note: B (bold, as in typefaces) moves from after R to after the new I

annotation.surface: A Balkan traveller forced to move on in search of a hostile place.
annotation.walkthrough: Put I into SERBIA after the S, then move the B (bold) to sit after that I: S-I-B-ERIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: the region stands for any remote, cold, unfriendly place, as in being sent to Siberia.

entries.clue: Colloquially, largest; most like the ocean? (7)

blocks.note: informal 'tidy' = sizeable, as in 'a tidy sum'
the ocean has tides, so the most tide-like body of water

annotation.walkthrough: Tidy in the sense 'sizeable' is informal, hence 'Colloquially'; the second reading makes tidy mean 'having tides'.
annotation.definitionFit: Colloquial sense: a tidy sum is a large one; the jokey second sense reads tidy as 'full of tides'.

entries.clue: Well-earnt rest, leisurely accepting support (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: the phrase takes the answer inside it

blocks.note: runs from the last letter of earnt, through rest, into the start of leisurely

annotation.surface: Someone taking a deserved break, happy to take a bit of help.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles three words, ignoring the comma.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain definition: a frame with splayed legs that supports a table top.

entries.clue: Some sets of twins resemble each other (7,5)

blocks.note: lookalikes, people who are each other's image
things alike are said to match

annotation.surface: A remark about how alike identical twins look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sets' reads as groups of twins, but it is tennis sets: a game for two pairs is played over sets. The whole clue looks like a single definition, which hides the charade.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tennis game between pairs is played as a number of sets.

entries.clue: Poems praising systems of regulation not started (4)

indicatorNotes.not started: the word never gets its first letter

annotation.surface: Verses written in praise of rules and regulations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Praising' belongs with 'Poems', not with the regulations it seems to describe.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an ode is a lyric poem addressed in praise of its subject.

entries.clue: Accept only part of repurchase agreement, being in the Black? (4)

indicatorNotes.Accept only part of: take only a section of the letters

blocks.note: runs across the end of repurchase and the first letter of agreement

annotation.surface: Financial jargon: agreeing to buy back part of a deal while staying in profit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the black' means in profit, but capitalised it is the Black Sea: being there is being out on the water.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: capital-B Black is the Black Sea, and being out on a sea is being at sea.

entries.clue: Trade ideas, wild wishes (10)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild letters run out of order

annotation.surface: Swapping fanciful dreams with each other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild wishes' reads as one phrase, but 'wild' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin plural meaning things desired, used in English for wishes or requirements.

entries.clue: Illegally assist a venture (4)

blocks.note: to venture money is to bet it

annotation.surface: Helping out with a risky scheme on the wrong side of the law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Illegally' matters: the word is specifically for helping with wrongdoing.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal term: to help or encourage someone to commit a crime.

entries.clue: Flights that may lead to landings? (10)

annotation.definition: Flights that may lead to landings?

blocks.note: not journeys by air but runs of steps between floors
not a plane touching down but the level floor at the top of the steps

annotation.surface: Air travel ending on a runway.
annotation.walkthrough: Flights and landings sound like aircraft, but a flight of stairs ends at a landing.
annotation.definitionFit: Pun: a flight is also a run of stairs, and a landing is the floor where it ends.

entries.clue: Step back, seeing Afghans, Abyssinians, etc? (4)

indicatorNotes.back: back = in reverse, so STEP is read from its end

annotation.surface: Retreating on meeting people from Afghanistan and Ethiopia.
annotation.walkthrough: Afghans and Abyssinians look like nationalities, but here they are an Afghan hound and an Abyssinian cat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Afghan hounds and Abyssinian cats are kept as domestic animals.
